beats.text: This is the Dreaming, where every dream begins. Aurie is its queen.
Her librarian, Lucienne, reads her the day's report. A nightmare has misbehaved.
Aurie closes her hand, and the nightmare is unmade.
Then, far away in the waking world, a man reads her name from a stolen book.
A circle of chalk reaches up through her floor, and pulls her down.
A cellar beneath Fawney Rig, the house of Roderick Burgess, magician.
His son Randall died in the war. Burgess wanted Death herself, to make her give him back.
But Death has a sister. Tonight his spell caught the wrong one.
Aurie wakes inside a sphere of glass, ringed by a circle she cannot cross.
His men carry off her three treasures: her helm, her pouch of sand, and her ruby.
Without them, she is only a prisoner.
Hours later, his followers have gone home. Burgess comes back down, alone.
He still believes he has caught Death. Speak to him, or stay silent. He will remember either way.

canon: The year is 1916. Burgess believes he has summoned Death and does not yet know this is Dream.
Aurie's helm, pouch of sand and ruby have already been taken from the circle and locked away.
Burgess wants three things: immortality, power, and the return of his son Randall who died at Gallipoli.
Burgess cannot open the sphere; the binding circle holds Aurie and only a broken circle frees her.
Aurie cannot be killed and cannot lie about what she is for long; the Endless are poor liars.

exits.1.2.A: Aurie refuses to speak at all and lets the silence answer him.
exits.1.2.B: Aurie threatens Burgess with what she will do to him when she is free.
exits.1.2.C: Aurie pretends to accept his bargain, promising him what he asks in exchange for freedom.
exits.1.2.D: Aurie tells him the truth: she is Dream of the Endless, not Death.

conversation.opening: You are awake. Good. I am Roderick Burgess, and you, creature, are mine. Give me what I want, and you will see daylight again. Immortality. Power. My son. Well?
possibilities: She mocks or threatens him: he hides his fear under ceremony, invokes the circle, and may order the wards doubled.
She speaks of his dead son: this is his wound; he grieves, then lashes out to cover it.
She tells him she is Dream, not Death: he is shaken, then greedy, and starts bargaining for dreams instead of death.
She bargains: he tests her, demands proof, and senses evasions, because the Endless lie badly.
She acts from inside the glass (candles gutter, the glass fogs, a nightmare touches him): he reacts physically and the cellar shows it.
She stays silent: he talks to fill the silence and reveals more than he means to.

NAMED_RANDALL.when: She speaks of his dead son Randall, by name or as his son, in a way that wounds or exposes him.
NAMED_RANDALL.ripple: For the first time, Burgess cannot hold your gaze.

echo.text: In 1916 the prisoner spoke of Randall to Roderick Burgess. He never said his son's name aloud again, and the house heard him weeping at night.

REVEALED_DREAM.when: She tells him plainly that she is Dream of the Endless, not Death.
REVEALED_DREAM.ripple: Somewhere in the house, every sleeper wakes at once.

echo.text: Roderick Burgess learned his prisoner was Dream, not Death, and spent his remaining years trying to buy dreams from her.

SHOWED_POWER.when: She acts on the world from inside the glass: guttering candles, fogging glass, a pressure in the air, a nightmare sent at him.
SHOWED_POWER.ripple: Burgess orders the wards doubled. The circle burns brighter, and the glass grows colder.

echo.text: In the first week the prisoner showed her power; Burgess doubled the wards and chained the cellar door.

PITIED_HIM.when: She shows him real pity or understanding for his grief.
PITIED_HIM.ripple: His hand hovers over the chalk line. Then he remembers himself.

echo.text: Once, early, the prisoner pitied Roderick Burgess, and he never forgave her for it.

choices.text: Say nothing. Just stare at him.

aftermath.text: You give him nothing. Not a word, not a flicker.
He leaves. He will come back every night for thirty years, and you will never answer him.

choices.text: When I am free, you will beg me for sleep.

aftermath.text: The candles lean away from the glass. Burgess stumbles back.
That night he doubles the wards. The circle burns colder, and you grow weaker.

choices.text: Free me, and you shall have everything you ask.

aftermath.text: He laughs, then stops. He knows a lie when he hears one.
From now on, he believes nothing you say.

choices.text: You fool. I am not Death. I am Dream, her sister.

aftermath.text: Burgess goes pale. Then, slowly, he smiles.
If he cannot have Death, he will have dreams instead. He will beg you for them for the rest of his life.

beats.text: Upstairs, Burgess never speaks his son's name again.
Every night he comes down to beg you for dreams. You give him none.
Once, early on, you pitied him. He never forgave you for it.
Without its queen, the Dreaming begins to fall apart. Her palace crumbles into sand.
In the waking world, sleep goes wrong. Some people can never sleep again.
Others fall asleep, and cannot wake. The doctors call it the sleeping sickness.
One of them is a girl in Kent named Unity Kincaid. Hers is the only dream Aurie can still reach.
Aurie reaches into the girl's sleep, and finds her waiting in a dream of the sea.

canon: Unity Kincaid fell into the sleeping sickness in 1916 at about ten years old. Her body has grown older in bed, but in her dream she is still a child.
Aurie is imprisoned in the glass sphere far away; her power only just reaches into one sleeping mind, this girl's.
Unity answers only as a dreaming child: drowsy, curious, unafraid, in dream logic.
Aurie cannot wake her and cannot escape through her.
Something else has been visiting Unity's dream, a perfumed presence she cannot name (in truth Desire of the Endless); Unity does not know what it is.
conversation.opening: Is somebody there? I can't wake up. It's ever so quiet here... and something keeps visiting me that isn't you. It smells of roses.
possibilities: She comforts the girl: Unity is soothed and the dream warms.
She promises something: Unity holds the promise tightly, as children do.
She gives her a good dream: the room fills with a place Unity loves.
She asks about the other visitor: Unity describes it innocently (roses, a smile, a glass heart), which should unsettle Aurie.
She tries to use the girl to escape, or commands her coldly: the dream turns grey and Unity is frightened.

exits.1.3.W: Aurie has given her something to keep in the long sleep (a promise, a gift, a warning), or says goodbye and withdraws from the dream.

UNITY_PROMISE.when: She promises to remember her, to return for her, or that her life will matter.
UNITY_PROMISE.ripple: In a sunlit room in Kent, a sleeping girl smiles.

echo.text: In 1916 Dream promised the sleeping girl Unity Kincaid she would not be forgotten. Unity carried that promise through sixty years of sleep.

UNITY_GIFT.when: She gives her a good dream to live in during the long sleep.
UNITY_GIFT.ripple: The girl's dream fills with sea air and gulls.

echo.text: Unity Kincaid slept for sixty years inside a seaside dream that Dream gave her in 1916.

UNITY_USED.when: She tries to use the girl as a way out, or commands her coldly.
UNITY_USED.ripple: The girl's dream turns grey at the edges.

echo.text: Dream once tried to use a sleeping child as a door. Unity Kincaid remembered the cold of it all her life.

SENSED_VISITOR.when: She asks about the other visitor, or searches the dream for who else is there.
SENSED_VISITOR.ripple: For an instant you smell a perfume you know. Then it is gone.

echo.text: Dream sensed another of the Endless inside Unity Kincaid's dream in 1916 and told no one.

choices.text: Say goodbye, and leave her dream.

aftermath.text: Unity will carry your promise through sixty years of sleep.
She sleeps on, inside the seaside dream you gave her.
Her dream stays grey for a long, long time.
And you cannot forget that smell of roses. Someone else was in that dream.
You let go of the girl. The glass closes around you again.

beats.text: Burgess's mistress, Ethel Cripps, runs away in the night.
She takes his money, and she takes your helm, your sand and your ruby.
Roderick Burgess dies an old man, still waiting for a wish you never granted.
His son Alex inherits the house, the order, and the prisoner in the cellar.
The wards are still doubled, as they have been since your first week.
Alex is grey now. He has never once been cruel to you. Tonight, for the first time, he has come down to talk.
Behind him, Paul, the man who loves him, pretends not to listen.

canon: It is the 1970s. Roderick Burgess died years ago; Alex inherited the house, the order and the prisoner.
Alex is frightened of Aurie and ashamed of his father. He has never once been cruel to her himself.
Paul McGuire is Alex's companion and guard and loves him; Paul will stop Alex from doing anything rash.
Alex could break the circle. He has thought about it for decades and never done it.
Aurie can show Alex a dream through the glass if she chooses; she cannot leave.

exits.1.4.A: Aurie shows Alex a dream of his father's cruelty to him as a boy, so he knows she sees him.
exits.1.4.B: Aurie stares through Alex and gives him nothing.
exits.1.4.C: Aurie shows Alex a vision of his own death.
exits.1.4.D: Aurie asks Alex to free her and swears he will come to no harm.

conversation.opening: I know you can hear me. I have always known. If I let you go... will you hurt me?
possibilities: She is kind: he softens, and may confess what he almost did in 1950.
She promises not to harm him: he holds onto it for years.
She threatens or horrifies him: he flees and stays away for a decade.
She speaks to Paul: Paul is moved, and becomes Alex's protector against her.
She asks about his father: he speaks of Roderick with fear and shame, drawing on whatever passed between his father and her.
She asks about her tools: he knows only that they vanished from the house when he was a boy.

ALEX_CONFESSED.when: She is kind enough that he admits he once almost broke the circle, in 1950.
ALEX_CONFESSED.ripple: Behind him, Paul looks away and says nothing.

echo.text: Alex Burgess confessed to the prisoner that in 1950 he stood at the circle with a wet cloth and could not wipe it away.

ALEX_PROMISE.when: She promises he will be safe from her, or that she will not harm him if he frees her.
ALEX_PROMISE.ripple: Afterwards he writes something down, and keeps it in his breast pocket.

echo.text: In the 1970s Dream promised Alex Burgess he would be safe from her.

ALEX_TERRIFIED.when: She threatens him or shows him horror.
ALEX_TERRIFIED.ripple: He does not come down to the cellar again for eleven years.

echo.text: The prisoner terrified Alex Burgess so badly that he stayed away from the cellar for eleven years.

PAUL_MOVED.when: She speaks to Paul directly, or appeals to his kindness.
PAUL_MOVED.ripple: Paul's hand closes, very gently, on Alex's shoulder.

echo.text: The prisoner once spoke to Paul McGuire directly, and Paul never forgot it.

choices.text: Show him the boy his father hurt, so he knows I see him.

aftermath.text: He weeps for the little boy his father hurt. No one has ever seen that boy but you.

choices.text: Give him nothing. Look straight through him.

aftermath.text: Nothing comes from the glass. He goes upstairs, and does not come down again for years.
He sees himself old and broken, in a wheelchair. He runs from the cellar, screaming.

choices.text: Free me, Alex, and I swear you will come to no harm.

aftermath.text: He almost does it. Then he loses his nerve, and walks away.
But he writes your promise down, and keeps it in his breast pocket for the rest of his life.

beats.text: Seventy-two years in the glass. Alex is an old man now.
Since the vision of his death, he has not come down to the cellar once.
Tonight, the young guard falls asleep against the glass. His breath fogs it.
A sleeping mind is a door. And Aurie is the queen of dreams.
She steps through his dream, and out of the glass. The circle crumbles to dust.
Alex hears the glass break. Paul wheels him down, and there she is.
In his breast pocket is a folded paper with your promise on it.

canon: It is 1988. Aurie has just escaped the sphere. She is free and fully able to punish him; he knows it.
Alex Burgess is seventy-two, in a wheelchair. Paul McGuire pushed him in and stands behind him.
Roderick Burgess died in 1947.
In 1926 Roderick's mistress, Ethel Cripps, stole the helm, the pouch of sand and the ruby and fled. Alex knows her name, not where the tools are now.
Alex never harmed the prisoner himself; he also never freed her.
conversation.opening: Please. Please, I never... it was my father, it was all my father. I kept you safe down here. I kept them from hurting you. What... what are you going to do to me?
possibilities: She asks about her tools: he gives her Ethel Cripps's name to save himself.
She brings up what happened in the 1970s (a promise, a confession, terror): he answers from that shared history.
She threatens him: if Paul is his ally, Paul steps between them.
She listens to his plea: he asks forgiveness and tells her what seventy years in that house did to him.
She stays silent: he babbles, bargains, and finally weeps.

exits.1.5.A: Aurie condemns him to eternal waking.
exits.1.5.B: Aurie gives him one night of nightmares and then lets it end.
exits.1.5.C: Aurie turns and walks away, leaving him to his fear.

LEARNED_ETHEL.when: She asks where her helm, pouch and ruby went, and he tells her about Ethel Cripps.
LEARNED_ETHEL.ripple: A name, at last: Ethel Cripps.

echo.text: Alex Burgess told Dream that Ethel Cripps stole her helm, pouch and ruby in 1926.

PAUL_STEPS_IN.when: She threatens Alex and Paul, who cares for him, steps between them.
PAUL_STEPS_IN.ripple: Paul steps in front of the wheelchair. His hands are shaking. He does not move.

echo.text: When Dream escaped in 1988, Paul McGuire stood between her and Alex Burgess.

PROMISE_INVOKED.when: Alex reminds her of the promise she made him in the 1970s, or she acknowledges it.
PROMISE_INVOKED.ripple: He holds out the folded paper with your promise on it.

HEARD_HIS_LIFE.when: She lets him tell her what seventy years in that house did to him.
HEARD_HIS_LIFE.ripple: For a moment he is only a frightened old man, and so are you, almost.

choices.text: Wake, Alex. Wake forever, each time into something worse.

effectsIf.ripple: You promised him. The Dreaming remembers.

aftermath.text: He wakes, and wakes, and wakes, each time into something worse. He will never sleep again.

choices.text: One night of nightmares. Then it ends.

aftermath.text: One night of nightmares, and then it is over. By morning he sleeps like a child.

choices.text: Turn and walk away. He is old, and already afraid.

effectsIf.ripple: You remember the wet cloth, and the circle he could not wipe away.

aftermath.text: You walk out without a word. Behind you, an old man weeps with relief.

beats.text: Free, but weak. No helm, no sand, no ruby. Aurie goes home.
The great gates of her realm are cracked. One lantern still burns.
Most of the Dreaming is gone. Only the library still stands.
On its far wall are three doors she has never seen before.
And you have a name to start your search: Ethel Cripps.

canon: Aurie has been gone seventy-two years. The Dreaming decayed without her; many dreams and nightmares fled or faded.
Lucienne is the librarian of the Dreaming and keeps every book ever dreamed, including those never written.
On the far wall are three great locked doors carved NEVERWHERE, CORALINE and THE ALCHEMIST. Lucienne knows they are stories and that they will open in time; she will hint but not explain.
Aurie's three tools are still missing: the helm, the pouch of sand, the ruby. Lucienne knows they were stolen from Burgess's house and scattered.
The reading table has four empty places; Lucienne says nothing about what belongs there yet.

exits.2.1.A: Aurie answers her coldly, as a queen to a servant, and demands a report.
exits.2.1.B: Aurie tells Lucienne she is sorry, thanks her for waiting, or confides in her.

conversation.opening: My lady. Seventy-two years. We thought... forgive me. We thought you were dead. The realm is not as you left it.
possibilities: She confides fear, weakness or grief: Lucienne softens and becomes her confidant.
She asks about the three doors: Lucienne hints and will not explain.
She asks where her tools are: Lucienne knows only what Aurie has learned, and says what the Dreaming lost without them.
She is cold or blames Lucienne for the decay: Lucienne reports with icy precision and is quietly hurt.
She asks what happened while she was gone: Lucienne reports the dead, the fled and the faithful, and anything she knows of Aurie's own deeds.

CONFIDED.when: She admits fear, weakness, grief or doubt to Lucienne.
CONFIDED.ripple: Lucienne takes off her spectacles, which she has never done in front of you.

ASKED_DOORS.when: She asks about the three locked doors.
ASKED_DOORS.ripple: The keyhole of the smallest door glows, very faintly, for one breath.

COLD_TO_LUCIENNE.when: She orders Lucienne about coldly, or blames her for the realm's decay.
COLD_TO_LUCIENNE.ripple: Lucienne's pen stops for a moment, then continues.

aftermath.text: Lucienne bows, and begins: the dead, the fled, and the faithful.

choices.text: I am sorry I was gone so long.

aftermath.text: Lucienne takes off her spectacles. For the first time in seventy-two years, she smiles.

beats.text: You are home. But you are not whole.
Your helm, your sand and your ruby are out there, scattered across the waking world.
Only three women know where every lost thing goes.
Behind the three doors, other stories are waiting for you.
End of Part One.
Lost things leave a trail, and only three women can read it.
Mortals call them the Fates. They are three, and they are one.
Aurie walks to the crossroads at the edge of her realm, and calls them.

canon: It is 1988, days after Aurie's escape. She is weak and has none of her three tools.
The Three answer at most three questions in one meeting, and they enjoy being asked politely.
The pouch of sand is in London, near a woman called Johanna Constantine; someone has been breathing the sand for years and it is killing them.
The helm was traded to a demon and is in Hell.
The ruby went from Ethel Cripps to her son John Dee, who is locked in a madhouse in America and still dreams of it.
conversation.opening: MAIDEN: Look who's come back! MOTHER: Thin as a rake, poor thing. CRONE: Three questions, dearie. Ask them nicely.
possibilities: She asks where her sand, helm or ruby is: they answer plainly, one each, in turn.
She asks which to seek first: the sand, because someone is dying of it.
She asks about her own fate: the crone answers with one short chilling riddle, and the others go quiet.
She is rude or commands them: they mock her, and the maiden stops smiling.
She thanks them, or offers something: they are delighted and bless her road.
suggestions: Where is my pouch of sand?
Tell me what becomes of me.

exits.2.2.GO: Aurie has her answers (or the three questions are spent) and sets off to find the sand in London.

ASKED_FATE.when: She asks what will become of her, or about her own future or death.
ASKED_FATE.ripple: The crone's shears close on nothing. You feel it in your chest.

echo.text: Dream asked the Three what would become of her, and the crone's answer chilled her.

RUDE_TO_THREE.when: She orders them about, threatens them, or is contemptuous.

THANKED_THREE.when: She thanks them sincerely, or offers them something in return.
THANKED_THREE.ripple: The crone cackles, pleased, and the moon grows brighter.

choices.text: Thank you, sisters. I will start with the sand.

aftermath.text: The sand is in London. The helm is in Hell. The ruby is with the son of Ethel Cripps.
And one answer she did not want.
The sand comes first. Someone is dying of it.

beats.text: The sand leads her to a rainy street in north London.
Someone is waiting there, as if she has been expecting trouble for years.
Johanna Constantine. Exorcist, chain-smoker, and the last person who held the pouch.

canon: London, 1988, after midnight, in the rain, outside a terraced house whose one upstairs window glows gold.
Rachel, Johanna's former lover, lives inside and has been breathing the sand for years; the house has turned into a dream.
Johanna knows what Aurie is. She will take her inside, but she wants Rachel treated gently.
conversation.opening: Well. You're real, then. You're after the sand, aren't you, love? It's up there, and so is Rachel. Whatever you do in that house, you do it gently.
possibilities: She asks about Rachel: Johanna tells her, and her jokes wear thin.
She is kind to Johanna: Johanna admits she loved Rachel and left her.
She is cold or threatening: Johanna is unimpressed and says so.
She asks what the sand does to a mortal: it gives them every dream at once, and eats them.
She agrees to go in: Johanna flicks away her cigarette and leads the way.
suggestions: What has my sand done to her?

exits.2.3.IN: Aurie goes into the house, with Johanna leading the way.

JOHANNA_CONFIDED.when: She is kind to Johanna or asks gently about Rachel, and Johanna admits she loved her and left.
JOHANNA_CONFIDED.ripple: Johanna looks away, up at the gold window.

echo.text: Johanna Constantine told Dream that she loved Rachel and left her when it got hard.

SCARED_JOHANNA.when: She threatens Johanna or shows her power to frighten her.
SCARED_JOHANNA.ripple: Every streetlight on the road goes out at once, then flickers back.

aftermath.text: Johanna flicks her cigarette into the gutter, and leads the way.

beats.text: Inside, the house has become a dream. It breathes.
Rachel has breathed the sand for years. It is the only thing keeping her alive, and it is killing her.
Without your ruby you cannot give her life back. Only an ending: a kind one, or a cruel one.

canon: They stand in Rachel's overgrown room. Rachel lies on the bed, wasted, dreaming, beyond speech.
When the pouch is taken back, Rachel will die. Aurie can make it gentle by giving her a last good dream, or simply take the pouch and let her die in pain.
Aurie does not have the power to save Rachel's life without her ruby, and Johanna knows it.
The ruby is not here: it is with John Dee in an American madhouse. Aurie holds only what she came with.
conversation.opening: Christ. Rach. Look at her. You can't fix this, can you? Then for God's sake, make it kind.
possibilities: She promises to be gentle, or gives Rachel a good dream: Johanna weeps quietly and thanks her, gruffly.
She takes the pouch coldly: Johanna is horrified and curses her.
She tries to save Rachel: she cannot; Johanna tells her not to drag it out.
She asks Johanna what Rachel loved: Johanna tells her about a summer, a garden, the two of them young.
suggestions: What did she love, when she was well?

exits.2.4.A: Aurie gives Rachel a gentle last dream and lets her die in peace.
exits.2.4.B: Aurie takes the pouch and leaves Rachel to die as she will.

HEARD_RACHEL.when: She asks Johanna what Rachel loved, and listens.
HEARD_RACHEL.ripple: For a moment the room smells of cut grass and summer.

choices.text: Give her one last good dream, and let her go in peace.

aftermath.text: You give Rachel a dream: a summer garden, and Johanna young beside her.
It is the garden Johanna told you about.
She dies smiling. The sand flows home into the pouch.
Johanna does not thank you. But she will remember this.

choices.text: Take the pouch. Her pain is not my concern.

aftermath.text: You take the pouch. Behind you, Rachel begins to scream.
Johanna's curse follows you all the way down the stairs.

beats.text: The pouch of sand is hers again. One of three.
She feels the Dreaming stir, a little stronger.
Next, the helm. In Hell.
